name: Bodyweight Forward Lunge
summary: A fundamental unilateral lower-body exercise where one leg steps forward, lowers until both knees bend, and drives back to the starting position.

setup: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, shoulders relaxed, and torso tall.
Place your hands firmly on your hips or clasp them loosely in front of your chest for balance.
steps: Take a controlled step forward with the working leg, maintaining hip-width spacing between your feet.
Lower your body under control until both knees are bent at roughly ninety degrees, with the back knee hovering just off the floor.
Drive firmly through the heel and midfoot of your front leg to push yourself straight back to the starting stance.
Repeat for the target number of repetitions on one side before switching to the opposite leg.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you step forward and lower down; exhale forcefully as you drive through the front foot to return to the standing position.

common_faults.fault: Stepping in-line as if on a tightrope, compromising lateral balance.
common_faults.correction: Keep feet hip-width apart throughout the movement as if standing on parallel railroad tracks.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the front knee to collapse inward during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Actively track the knee over the second and third toes of the lead foot.

common_faults.fault: Slamming the rear knee into the floor.
common_faults.correction: Decelerate smoothly and reverse the motion when the trailing knee is about an inch above the ground.

precautions: Ensure the floor is clean and non-slippery to prevent foot sliding on impact.
